title: Apple Music to Label AI-Made Tracks Later This Year
description:
Apple Music will begin labeling songs on the platform derived from AI platforms, adding a “Made With AI” label to such songs later this year.

	In a
body:
Apple Music will begin labeling songs on the platform derived from AI platforms, adding a “Made With AI” label to such songs later this year.

	In a note to its industry partners and one viewed by Variety, the service said that record labels and distributors will be required to tag songs in which “a material portion of the content” was created using AI. The labels follow Apple Music’s introduction in March of AI Transparency Tagging, which dictates in the service’s systems whether a track used AI.
	

	“As we implement Made With AI Labels, content providers will be important partners,” Apple Music said. “They are best positioned to know how their content was created, and the AI Transparency Tags that should be used.”


	It was unclear when the new labels would begin to appear on the streamer. Record labels and the streaming services they feed have spent the last three years navigating the rise of AI music generators such as Suno and Udio, opting between litigation to licensing deals to developing competing tools, such as remixing products. 

	The announcement follows Spotify’s decision to label the profiles of artists who appear to be AI-generated as “AI Personas” and Tidal’s decision to label AI music and ban those tracks from accruing royalties. A collection of groups representing musicians and the music industry at large — including the RIAA, IFPI, the Grammys and SAG-AFTRA — also banded together last month to advocate for a new labeling program to indicate whether a song has been produced with AI.

	Apple Music vice president Oliver Schusser told Billboard earlier this year that “more than a third” of the tracks uploaded to the platform were “100% AI.” He added that, while the company had in-house detection software to screen songs and determine how AI was used and what models created them, it was up to those who upload tracks to “take responsibility“ for disclosing the use of AI.
	

	“You should know that every label in the world is delivering AI, [even if] they might not know about it,” he said. “They themselves also need to develop tools to understand [the scope of AI use].”

title: Sonic the Hedgehog to Headline Fortnite’s ‘Override’ Season (Gaming News Roundup)
description:
Sonic the Hedgehog will headline Fortnite’s new “Override” season. 

	Players will be able to play as Sonic and unlock the Tails Sidekick with the p
body:
Sonic the Hedgehog will headline Fortnite’s new “Override” season. 

	Players will be able to play as Sonic and unlock the Tails Sidekick with the purchase of the Battle Pass for the hedgehog’s 35th anniversary. The collaboration will also feature the Tails Sprite, Rings and Sonic Power Sneakers, which allows players to Spin Dash in their fight against Dr. Eggman. 

	“Bringing Sonic and his friends into Fortnite gives generations of fans an exciting new way to experience these beloved characters together and serves as another major moment in Sonic’s 35th anniversary,” Takashi Iizuka, Sonic Creative Officer, Sega of America, Inc., tells Variety. 
	

	The “Override” season also includes classic video game mechanics, such as Cheat Codes and 1-Up Tokens. 


	See more gaming news from this week in the roundup below.
	
		IN-GAME EVENTS	

	Get in, losers! It’s time to take your Sim shopping.

	“The Sims 4” is getting two new for-purchase fashion kits for “Mean Girls” and “Clueless,” upgrading players’ online closets with ‘90s and early 2000s looks. 

	Starting Aug. 27, the Mean Girls Capsule will bring a fetch array of miniskirts and matching sweaters and velour track suits, plus looks inspired by some of the film’s most notable scenes: the jingle bell performance and Mathletes team jacket. The Clueless Capsule Kit will feature Cher’s infamous yellow-plaid set, layered tops, button-front skirts, workout wear and overalls inspired by Tai. 

	Think you won’t have enough to wear after these fashion kits? Ugh! As if!
	



	

	





	

	



	*

	“Game of Thrones: Dragonfire” is adding a limited-time “House of the Dragon” event to celebrate the series finale.

	Available now until Aug. 24, all dragons released throughout Season 3 are back at the Hatchery. The dragons are identical to those seen on screen and each possess unique passive Habit abilities, troop affinities and powerful synergies. They will return to standard drop rates following the limited-time event.

	Players can link their HBO Max and Warner Bros. Games accounts to “Game of Thrones: Dragonfire” to earn rewards by watching the third season of “House of the Dragon” until Oct. 1.
	
		TABLE-TOP CARD/RPG	

	Ravensburger announced a digital version of Disney Lorcana Trading Card Game (TCG) is officially in the works. 

	While at D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event, Ravensburger shared Disney Lorcana TCG will be featured at more Disney events and theme parks starting 2027, including exclusive cards at Epcot’s International Festival of the Arts. It is also set to expand across the Disney Cruise Line with its Collection Quests. 

	Curator’s Collection Beauty and the Beast Edition, the new addition to the Curator’s Collection line, will release this October at select Disney locations and will feature new artwork of the film’s characters.

	The digital version of Disney Lorcana TCG will be playable on desktop and mobile. Fans can check its status on the Disney Lorcana website.
	
		DELAYS	

	The Esports Foundation (EF) has postponed the inaugural Esports Nations Cup until November 2027. 

	Originally planned to take place in November 2026, the event date was changed after “ongoing assessment of the wider regional situation.”

	“The decision to postpone the Esports Nations Cup was not taken lightly,” said Ralf Reichert, CEO of the Esports Foundation. “The response from National Team Partners, publishers, players and communities around the world has shown us how much potential this competition has. We owe them an inaugural ENC delivered under the right conditions and at the level this idea deserves.” 

	The Esports Foundation (EF) is a non-profit organization based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia that aims to develop global gaming and esports. The Esports Nations Cup (ENC) is a global international esports competition for nations and territories. 
	
	
		EXEC SHUFFLE/LAYOFFS	

	New game studio Black Pony Immersive launched from game developers Harvey Smith and Ben Horne.

	The studio is built to design and develop first-person action RPGs where players can create their own experiences with emergent game systems.

	Smith serves as CEO and creative director for Black Pony Immersive. Horne is the chief operating officer and executive producer. Ricardo Bare is the design director.

	Smith served as studio director at Arkane Austin and is known for his work on the “Deus Ex” and “Dishonored” game series. Horne served as production director at Arkane Austin. Bare was most recently creative director at Arkane Studios and has worked as a designer on franchises including “Deus Ex” and “Prey.”
	
		RELEASE DATES	

	Construction sites just got a whole lot scarier. Dumb Ways To Die is launching even more ways to die with their latest spin-off game “Dumb Ways to Build” on Sept. 10.

	Players can wield a physics-based arsenal of tools to build construction sites and improvise their way out of chaotic and fatal situations. Whether tackling the job site with up to four friends in an online crew or braving it alone in Solo Play, the game puts your building and survival skills to the test.

	The game will be available across PC via Steam, PlayStation 5 and Xbox X|S for USD $7.99.

title: How an Indie Studio Convinced ‘Naruto’ Creator, TV Tokyo to Let Them Make Franchise’s First Official Digital Cards App (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Naruto” fans will have access to the popular anime franchise’s first-ever official digital cards app with Thursday’s worldwide launch of “Naruto Ni
body:
“Naruto” fans will have access to the popular anime franchise’s first-ever official digital cards app with Thursday’s worldwide launch of “Naruto Ninja Cards.”

	Described as “a gamified card-collecting experience,” “Naruto Ninja Cards” lets app users collect the series’ most iconic characters in card form, uncover exclusive artworks, and enjoy real-time strategic activities with friends.


	While the offering, the only free-to-play “Naruto” app on the App Store and Google Play, may seem like a small-scale project, the app has been five years in the making for Paris and Tokyo-based indie studio Sekai.
	

	After launching as an anime-focused startup in 2021 and a few rounds of brainstorming and development talks, the initial four-person Sekai team set out to land the rights to make a “Naruto” app from Japanese broadcaster TV Tokyo. (There have been many unofficial “Naruto” apps and projects launched over the years, but few approved by the IP owner.) The network not only ended up partnering with Sekai, but also invested in the studio, marking its first investment in a Western company since it backed Crunchyroll. 


	“We spent a year and a half in Japan convincing the IP’s owners to trust us, and became the first foreign studio ever licensed to build this,” Samy Therain, cofounder and CEO of Sekai, says. “We’re giving our soul to this project. Half a million fans felt it, and showed up before we ever asked. Today’s launch is theirs.”



	

					TV Tokyo/Sekai
	



	“The Sekai team’s genuine passion for ‘Naruto’ is what truly resonates with fans worldwide,” TV Tokyo head of global distribution Hiroaki Saiki says. “I trust that their care, patience, and deep understanding of the series’ core spirit will drive the success of this product!”
	

	 Sekai’s investors also include Mike Shinoda of Linkin Park (a band whose music is closely tied to the “Naruto” fan-edit community), NBA All-Star Rudy Gobert, Skycatcher, Makers Fund and Alexis Ohanian’s fund 776.

	According to Sekai, since “Naruto Ninja Cards” soft launched Feb. 5 the app has seen 500,000 downloads, 93% of which it says is from organic search. The team credits its early success to “never-before-seen hand-drawn artworks, Easter eggs hidden for those who know the series by heart, and updates shaped by fan feedback since day one.”

	Though today is the worldwide launch for “Naruto Ninja Cards,” just a few years ago the Sekai team was mourning the project before it even got off the ground.

	After months of grinding at licensing expos and networking events, a chain-reaction of high-profile introductions (including meetings with Reddit founder Alexis Ohanian, Crunchyroll founder Kun Gao and former Toei Animation boss Kanji Kazahaya) Therain says Sekai had its first sit-down with the TV Tokyo team in January 2022. Over the course of a year and a half living in Japan and months of discussion and negotiations and relationship-building with TV Tokyo, Therain says Sekai was “ghosted” by the network and didn’t know why. 



	

					TV Tokyo/Sekai
	



	From here, Sekai plans to not only grow the “Naruto Ninja Cards” app, but also expand into anime-inspired AAA games and even live events.

	“When they don’t reply to one email, you know something is wrong, and so that’s what happened. And for a month, we had no news,” Therain tells Variety. “So that’s why I flew. I flew again to Japan, and I wanted to get a chance to go to them. That’s why my hotel room was across the street from their office because I knew, when I’m there, I need to be available if they want to talk to me. I’m right across the street, and so we went there with two of my co-founders and we waited a bit.”

	The rain says the Sekai team received guidance from industry insiders that this turn of events likely meant the deal was going to “fade away.” Then they learned “Naruto” author Masashi Kishimoto had not signed off on the project.



	

					Sekai leadership team/Courtesy Sekai
	



	“And then I get a call telling me it’s over,” Therain says. “Then I’m like, what can we do? It’s either we start with another IP from the ground up, and so it’s going to take a lot more time, or I don’t know — find something, do something.”
	

	The Sekai team was at a loss, and Therain recalls calling his wife crying in the lobby of a hotel in Tokyo.

	“The dream is over. It’s over. It’s just over. And she’s like, ‘What? Why? What happened?’ So I tell her, ‘The author said no,’” Therain says. “And you can’t talk to the author. You can’t get an audience with him. Once he says no, goodbye. And she’s like, ‘That’s great news!’ I’m like, ‘What didn’t you understand? The author said no.’ And she reminded me that the entire adventure was under the, let’s say the protection of Naruto, and our motto as a company was ‘Live your own shonen adventure’ or ‘Live like a shonen,’ which literally means when something goes bad, just fight for it.’” 

	The rain says his wife inspired him to keep trying and “so I just went home, and I wrote a letter to the author of ‘Naruto,’ not knowing if he would get it or read it or anything, I just put it on paper.”

	“Because that’s what Naruto does. Naruto is famous for what we call talk no jutsu, which is literally the power of words,” Therain says. “And so, whenever he beats an enemy, it’s never with his fists. It’s after they exhausted all the weaponry and the magic and all this stuff. That’s when they start talking, and he turns the bad guy into a good guy because in ‘Naruto,’ no bad guy is bad entirely. You can turn anything into anything else. So I wrote on paper what ‘Naruto’ meant to me, every reason why I loved him, and how he changed my life, how he was there all the time, every time. And I ended it with [a part] which was exactly like Naruto: “I don’t know if you’re going to say like ‘Sorry, yeah,’ but no matter what happens, basically I will try again and again and again. Akiramenai, I will never give up because this is my ninja way. And this is what you taught me with ‘Naruto,’ Sensei.’” 

	The rain says he can’t disclose what exactly happened from there, but notes that after he sent the letter to TV Tokyo, the deal was approved by “Naruto” author Masashi Kishimoto.

	“It was a beautiful loop, in a way, because I was in this moment where everything seemed lost, and I felt like Naruto, and I was listening to the music and I was crying because I was like, this is just reality matching with the dream,” Therain says. “So after that, the dream came true, basically.”
	

	“Until the end of this year, it’s mainly two things: product iterations, to bringing more and more and more. On Discord, we have almost 1,410 people, and we’re known to reply to everyone to take into account what they ask for, to steer the product into the direction of what people really want, so there’s a lot of product shipping,” Therain says. “Obviously, we’re shipping a new set of cards every three months, and that’s a lot of work. So shipping more cards so that more people see their favorite characters that they can have, and they and they are happy about that. And then communication.” 

	The next part of the plan is “doing more stuff around ‘Naruto’ because our IP deal covers more.”

	“So one of them is live events in stadiums like no one has ever seen before, and so we’re already working on that with people from Hollywood and backers,” Therain says. “But we really want to create events that will feel to people after they participated in these events that they can’t go to any other type of event ever again. We call that the ‘Super Bowl of Anime.’ So we really, really want to bring the epicness that we feel when we watch a Naruto fight to a real live stage, and that obviously involves pyrotechnic effects, holograms, and things like that. That’s very important to us.”

schema.headline: How an Indie Studio Convinced ‘Naruto’ Creator, TV Tokyo to Let Them Make Franchise’s First Official Digital Cards App (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Netflix, AMC Team for ‘Bannerman’ Series Based on John R. Maxim Spy Novels, Shane Black and Craig Silverstein to Write
description: Netflix and AMC Studios are set to co-produce the drama series “Bannerman,” Variety has learned. The series is based on John R. Maxim’s Paul Bannerm
body:
Netflix and AMC Studios are set to co-produce the drama series “Bannerman,” Variety has learned. The series is based on John R. Maxim’s Paul Bannerman novels, of which five were published. 

	This marks the first Netflix/AMC Studios co-production. The show will air on AMC in the US and Canada and then become available on Netflix in those markets 90 days after the season finale. Netflix and AMC together will premiere each episode in Australia, New Zealand and Spain. Netflix will air the show exclusively in all other territories.
	

	The logline for “Bannerman” states, “Paul Bannerman, a lethal covert operative, convinces a group of the world’s most deadly assassins to quit the spy game for a chance to lead normal lives in the suburbs of Connecticut. Old enemies, bad habits, a paranoid government and an unrelenting ex-cop will make retirement their most difficult mission yet.” 


	Shane Black co-wrote the first episode with Craig Silverstein. Both serve as executive producers, with Silverstein also showrunning and with Black also directing. Greg Nicotero (“The Walking Dead,” “Creepshow,” “Pulp Fiction”) and Brian Witten (“Creepshow”) also executive produce. AMC Studios is the lead studio. 

	“’Bannerman’ is a smart, high-octane thrill ride of a series, powered by an extraordinary creative team,” said Dan McDermott, chief content officer of AMC Global Media and president of AMC Studios. “This is the perfect premium drama to kick off our first co-production with Netflix, and we are thrilled to continue evolving and expanding our partnership by jointly developing and producing select original series for our respective platforms.” 
	

	The first Bannerman novel, “The Bannerman Solution,” was published in 1989. That was followed by “The Bannerman Effect,” “Bannerman’s Law,” and “Bannerman’s Promise.” The final novel, “Bannerman’s Ghosts,” came out in 2003. 

	Silverstein previously created the AMC series “Turn: Washington’s Spies” as well as the animated AMC series “Pantheon.” He is also known for creating or co-creating shows like “Terra Nova” and “Nikkita,” while his other credits include “Bones,” “The Old Man.” He is an executive producer and co-showrunner on Disney+’s “Percy Jackson and the Olympians.” 

	“Bannerman” marks the first TV writing credit of Black’s career, though he did receive a credit for creating the character’s on which Fox’s “Lethal Weapon” TV show was based. Aside from “Lethal Weapon,” he is known for writing movies like “The Nice Guys,” “Kiss Kiss Bang Bang,” “Iron Man 3,” and “Last Action Hero.” 

	Silverstein is repped by WME and Hansen Jacobson. Black is repped by WME, Greenlit, and Eric Brooks. Nicotero is repped by UTA, Mosaic, and JSSK. Witten is repped by UTA and Mosaic.

	This marks the latest example of a TV show based on a multi-part book series. Streamers have found great success with such shows in recent years, including hits like “Bridgerton” (Netflix), “The Lincoln Lawyer” (Netflix), “Virgin River” (Netflix), “Reacher” (Amazon), “Slow Horses” (Apple TV), and “Off Campus” (Amazon).

schema.headline: Netflix, AMC Team for ‘Bannerman’ Series Based on John R. Maxim Spy Novels, Shane Black and Craig Silverstein to Write

title: CBS Plans Special Morning, Primetime Coverage of 9/11 Anniversary
description: CBS will fill key morning and primetime hours on September 11 with live coverage and special programming devoted to the 25th anniversary of terroris
body:
CBS will fill key morning and primetime hours on September 11 with live coverage and special programming devoted to the 25th anniversary of terrorist attacks on America on that date in 2001.

	The CBS programming will also be available on Paramount+. A selection of reporting on the attacks and their aftermath from “60 Minutes” will be featured  on CBSNews.com, Paramount+ and CBS News‘ YouTube channel. The 59th season of “60 Minutes” is slated to commence on Sunday, September 13.
	

	CBS’ efforts will join those of ABC News, NBC News, Fox News Channel, MS NOW and CNN. The 25th anniversary of the attacks has spurred many news organizations to offer a broader array of programming, which in most years is largely tied to comemmoration.


	CBS News will start coverage on “CBS Mornings,” which will feature co-hosts Gayle King and Nate Burleson along with “CBS Evening News” anchor Tony Dokoupil at Ground Zero in New York and “60 Minutes” correspondent Norah O’Donnell reporting from the Pentagon. Dokoupil and O’Donnell will launch a 90 minute special report at 8:30 a.m. that covers memorials occurring in New York, Shanksville and the Pentagon. CBS News correspondents will report from New York City, the Pentagon and the site of the crash of Flight 93 near Shanksville.

	Dokoupil will return at 6:30 p.m. to anchor “CBS Evening News” live from Ground Zero.

	He will also anchor at 8 p.m. “We Remember,” a special from Ground Zero that will feature three stories tied to the tragedy. Lesley Stahl of “60 Minutes” will revisit a story from the newsmagazine, reported by her late colleague Ed Bradley, that looks at Summit, N.J., which lost nine residents in the attacks. Stahl will add to the report with details  on how the town is coping with its history. Dokoupil will speak with a family that escaped the World Trade Center with their toddler but lost their patriarch, while O’Donnell will interview General Dan Caine, chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff.
	

	CBS will present “Daughters of 9/11” at 9 p.m., during which Elizabeth Miller, Jessica Trant and FBI special agent Frank Pellegrino probe whether the man accused of masterminding the attacks, Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, will ever face justice.

	· CBSNews.com, Paramount+ and CBS News’ YouTube channel will also showcase a selection of 60 MINUTES’ best reporting on the 9/11 attacks and their aftermath over the past 25 years.

	· CBS New York will have extensive multiplatform coverage, including more than two dozen stories on the attacks and recovery, among them, an explainer from its state-of-the-art Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality-driven studio that showcases the rebuilding of the World Trade Center campus. Kristine Johnson and Jessica Moore will anchor a one-hour special from the 9/11 Memorial on Thursday, Sept. 10. The station will feature anchored coverage of the memorial on Friday, Sept. 11.

	· CBS News 24/7 will provide comprehensive coverage all day, beginning at 7:00 AM, ET. CBS News 24/7 will stream the 90-minute special report at 8:30 AM, ET, followed by continuing live coverage from 10:00 AM-12:00 PM, ET. Expanding on CBS News’ original reporting, CBS News 24/7 will feature interviews with newsmakers, analysts and those impacted by the attacks, to assess the U.S. standing 25 years later and what is at stake globally. CBS News 24/7 will also present 9:11: WE REMEMBER, a CBS News special, the weekend of Sept. 1

schema.headline: CBS Plans Special Morning, Primetime Coverage of 9/11 Anniversary

title: Charles Melton in Talks for ‘Naruto’ Movie as Kakashi
description:
Charles Melton is in close talks to play Kakashi Hatake in Destin Daniel Cretton’s upcoming live-action “Naruto” movie, Variety has learned.

	The n
body:
Charles Melton is in close talks to play Kakashi Hatake in Destin Daniel Cretton’s upcoming live-action “Naruto” movie, Variety has learned.

	The news comes amid speculation that Melton would be announced to join the “X-Men” cast at last week’s D23 convention. The global “Naruto” casting search began last month to find the live-action versions of Naruto, Sasuke and Sakura. The manga and popular anime series follow adolescent ninja Naruto, who dreams of becoming his community’s protector and leader known as the village ninja.
	

	Variety has reached out to Lionsgate for comment.


	Melton was recently Emmy-nominated for his role in Netflix’s “Beef” Season 2 alongside Oscar Isaac, Carey Mulligan and Cailee Spaeny. He received critical acclaim for his work in Todd Haynes’ “May December,” which released in 2023, and is also known for starring in “Her Private Hell,” “Warfare” and “Riverdale.”

	Cretton is coming off of his box-office smash hit “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which has grossed over $800 million domestically, becoming the fastest film to ever hit the milestone.

	The “Naruto” director got his start working in the indie film space with “Short Term 12,” which released in 2013 and starred Brie Larson, LaKeith Stanfield, Rami Malek and Kaitlyn Dever. After directing “The Glass Castle” and “Just Mercy,” he made the leap to big-budget studio films with Marvel’s “Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings,” which released in 2021.

	Avi Arad, Ari Arad and Emmy Yu will produce “Naruto” for Arad Productions with Jeremy Latcham. Cretton is producing alongside Jeyun Munford through his company, Hisako. Back in 2014, there was an attempt to get a “Naruto” movie off the ground with Michael Gracey attached as director.

schema.headline: Charles Melton in Talks for ‘Naruto’ Movie as Kakashi

title: How This Year’s Drama Nominees, From ‘Paradise’ to ‘The Pitt,’ Tackle Our Troubled Times
description: I must confess, one of the appeals of Apple TV’s Emmy-nominated “Your Friends & Neighbors” is seeing how awful it is to be that wealthy. I mean, it’
body:
I must confess, one of the appeals of Apple TV’s Emmy-nominated “Your Friends & Neighbors” is seeing how awful it is to be that wealthy. I mean, it’s a TV show, so I’m guessing it’s actually still pretty awesome to be rich. (And if you’re still a Variety subscriber and reading this in print, there’s a good chance you made it big in entertainment and are sitting on a hefty bank account. And if so, congratulations. I still want to be you.)
	

	“Your Friends & Neighbors” gives us a glimpse of what it’s like to be in the 1%, especially in Season 2, as James Marsden joins the cast as a billionaire with plenty of questionable morals. At a time, of course, when it seems like all we’re confronting are billionaires with questionable morals who are taking over the government, the media and everything in between.


	But are they truly happy? Sure, there’s occasional nuisance — on “Your Friends & Neighbors,” it’s Jon Hamm stealing some of their loot; in real life, it’s state attorneys general trying to slow down your desire to consume as much of Hollywood as possible. But the answer is yes, yes they are.

	How upside down is this world now? HBO Max’s “The Gilded Age” is actually now wish fulfillment compared to 2026. OK, so there was great inequality, rampant corruption and poverty throughout much of the country even as America boomed in the 1880s — but at least the tycoons, magnates and moguls of the era at least pretended to care about the lower class. The Carnegies, the Vanderbilts, the Rockefellers all funded stuff that was good for the public, including public libraries, education, medicine, science, parks and culture.
	

	These days, they slam rockets into the side of the moon because it sounds cool and shut down global agencies meant to save the lives of millions of people. Or they stomp their feet and whine that they’re going to leave California if they don’t get their way. That “Gilded Age” sequel about the 2020s is gonna look a lot more like a tragedy.

	It turns out most of this year’s outstanding drama series nominees at the Emmys have something to say about the state of our world, and it’s pretty telling that there’s so much to talk about. In the case of Apple TV’s “Pluribus,” creator Vince Gilligan has still not confirmed if the drama is a comment on artificial intelligence, or even inspired by it. But he doesn’t have to — viewers are connecting the dots that may or may not be there, and applying their fear of AI to the show.

	HBO’s “A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms” might not overtly look like it has something to say about our present times, but it absolutely looks at the plight of ordinary people vs. the elites, and the exploitation of the working class.

	Meanwhile, Netflix’s “The Diplomat” and Apple TV’s “Slow Horses” look at the decay of our global order and a lack of moral clarity — and just look around our real world, with the current White House administration cozying up to despots and authoritarians. Who’s there even to root for anymore?

	HBO Max’s “The Pitt” continues to shine a light on the plight of first responders and the difficulties that medical workers face, while also amplifying the failures of America’s broken healthcare system. And star Noah Wyle tells me he’s hearing anecdotal evidence that it’s having an effect: “An attending physician in an emergency room here in Los Angeles wanted me to know that people are being nicer, and they’re treating their nurses and doctors with more kindness and more empathy,” he says. “And he thinks that’s a direct result of the show.”

	Then there’s Hulu’s “Paradise,” which starts out with an apocalyptic event brought on by climate change — in this case, a dormant supervolcano unleashed by melting ice. The show’s original idea of a peaceful city built underground to avoid the devastating global disaster is a bit far-fetched, but the causes behind a global crisis aren’t. And as we watch Europe burn this summer and face more record-breaking temperatures here in the U.S., it’s a reminder that climate change is the most important issue of our time — and one that the entertainment biz can’t ignore. Says “Paradise” writer Stephen Markley: “The biggest story to ever unfold in human history is happening right now, and Hollywood is barely breathing a word about it.”

schema.headline: How This Year’s Drama Nominees, From ‘Paradise’ to ‘The Pitt,’ Tackle Our Troubled Times

title: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Says the ‘Optics’ at Marvel Are ‘Obvious’ After ‘Wonder Man’ and ‘Blade’ Canceled: ‘If I’m Disney, I Do Not Want to Be Attached To These Optics’
description: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II says the “optics” at Marvel are obvious after the studio canceled his Emmy-nominated series “Wonder Woman” after one season an
body:
Yahya Abdul-Mateen II says the “optics” at Marvel are obvious after the studio canceled his Emmy-nominated series “Wonder Woman” after one season and failed over multiple years to bring to life the “Blade” movie it announced starring Mahershala Ali. Marvel canceled “Wonder Man” in July after previously renewing the series for Season 2. The show’s first season launched in January on Disney+.

	“I was told that it had something to do with the viewership numbers,” Abdul-Mateen recently told Vanity Fair. “I wasn’t told what those numbers were, but ultimately, for whatever reason it was, I think they decided that it didn’t make sense for business, and that’s the decision that we live with and we keep on marching forward.”
	

	When Vanity Fair mentioned the online discourse surrounding Marvel’s failure with two Black-led superhero projects (Ali called out Marvel in July for failing to develop his “Blade” movie), Abdul-Mateen responded: “I think the optics are obvious. If I’m a big business, if I’m Disney, if I’m Marvel, I don’t want to be attached to these optics.”

	“It should be a priority to change that narrative and to do what it takes to responsibly change that narrative with quality stories, with quality resources,” the actor continued. “I felt that our show did have quality story, did have quality resources, did have quality actors and people, and did produce quality results that the viewers responded to positively, that the voters responded to positively. So our show does deserve some study and some real, hard information about why a show like this did not continue forward, because it had all of the ingredients that one would want in a show.”
	

	Abdul-Mateen, who picked up an Emmy nomination for his role on “Wonder Man,” originally reacted to the show’s cancellation on Instagram, writing: “That’s life, right? Everything will shake out.”

	“The show worked. And that’s my favorite thing about it,” he added at the time. “I could see it on the faces of the Youtube Reactors (because I watched along with y’all this time. Shoutout to y’all) and I can see in the messages I get saying how the show reminded some of you not to give up, and I feel it in the genuine love shared when I bump into some of you all during the day. So, thinking of you all today.”

	Abdul-Mateen starred in “Wonder Man” as Simon Williams, an aspiring actor hiding his superpowers. Ben Kingsley reprised his role as Trevor Slattery after previous MCU outings. “Wonder Man” was created by Destin Daniel Cretton and Andrew Guest, with Cretton also directing the first two episodes. 

	Ali’s “Blade” movie was announced by Marvel at Comic-Con in 2019, but the movie failed to go into production after numerous starts and stops in the writing process. Several directors came and went form the project, from Bassam Tariq to Yann Damange. Ali told GQ he was training for over a year for “Blade” and then the movie never materialized. 

	“If they wanted to do it, we would’ve done it,” Ali said. “So I have to move on, and I have moved on. Again, you had me under contract, they have billions of dollars, if they wanted to do the movie, we would’ve done the movie. So we’re not doing the movie.”

	Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige said on the “Happy Sad Confused” last month that he feel like “a gigantic loser and failure” for not following through on Ali’s “Blade” movie.

schema.headline: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Says the ‘Optics’ at Marvel Are ‘Obvious’ After ‘Wonder Man’ and ‘Blade’ Canceled: ‘If I’m Disney, I Do Not Want to Be Attached To These Optics’

title: What Does Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s Move Back to the U.K. Mean for the Royal Family?
description: The Sussexes are coming home. In a shock announcement on Wednesday, it was revealed that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are moving back to the U.K.
body:
The Sussexes are coming home. In a shock announcement on Wednesday, it was revealed that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are moving back to the U.K. for an “extended period” with their two young children after six years of living in California. 

	But after the pair’s dramatic exit from royal life in 2020, will England — and the rest of their family — welcome them back with open arms?


	According to the BBC, Harry and Meghan’s decision to move back was made relatively recently, with King Charles only being informed of the news on Sunday. Their visit to the U.K. in July was a turning point, royal watchers believe, as they spent time with the King and also the family of Harry’s late mother Princess Diana, some of whom 7-year-old Archie and 5-year-old Lilibet met for the first time.
	

	“I think they had a really good trip here in the summer,” Sky News royal reporter, Laura Bundock, tells Variety. “Harry isn’t homesick, but I certainly think he wants his kids to understand more about British history and his homeland.”

	Their children’s education has also been a consideration for the move. The BBC said that Archie and Lilibet have both been enrolled in school in the U.K., and as most new terms start by mid-September, it’s expected that the family will settle in over the next couple of weeks.

	Though the King has welcomed the move to spend more time with Harry and his family, the BBC reported that it was a surprise to him and he had no involvement in the decision. King Charles was diagnosed with cancer in 2024, and though his treatment is said to be going well, Harry admitted in a BBC interview last year that he wanted to reconcile with him, saying: “I don’t know how much longer my father has.” 
	

	Harry’s brother, Prince William, is a different story. The two’s relationship has been said to be severely damaged following the 2023 publication of Harry’s memoir, “Spare,” and the bombshell 2021 interview he and Meghan did with Oprah Winfrey in which they leveled allegations of racism and mistreatment against unnamed members of the royal family. “Their friendship circles and acquaintances overlap to some extent,” says Bundock. “But I think to say that this is a moment of great reconciliation between those feuding brothers is far from reality.”

	Harry and Meghan’s announcement on Wednesday also made it clear that they will not be returning to their royal duties in any capacity now that they will be living in the U.K. They will live as private citizens — likely outside of London, according to the BBC — and continue their endeavors in production with Archewell as well as Meghan’s lifestyle brand As Ever. It’s possible they could expand these operations outside of the U.S., but they will stay headquartered in America. They also will not be selling their Montecito home, leaving the door open for an eventual return.

	But as Bundock points out, when Harry is carrying out philanthropic endeavours in the U.K., it may not always be obvious to the casual observer that he is not technically there in a royal capacity. “When you’re looking at Harry, for example, on an Invictus [Games] engagement, it looks, to all intents and purposes, like a royal engagement. He is still a member of the royal family. He’s just not a working royal.” It’s a situation that may well cause tension within the royal households, particularly as the senior royals coordinate their diaries behind the scenes (to ensure no one steals the limelight from each other) in deference to the King.

	While Harry and Meghan’s Hollywood ambitions were said to be a key reason behind their original move to California, Archewell Productions and its deal with Netflix has been the subject of scrutiny in recent years. Though the pact remains in tact, sources told Variety in a story about the couple’s deal with the streamer: “The mood in the building is, ‘We’re done.'” (In March, it was announced that the duo is developing a film adaptation of the Afghan war memoir “No Way Out: The Searing True Story of Men Under Siege” for Netflix.) Other lucrative opportunities have also fallen by the wayside, including a deal with Spotify reported to be worth $20 million that yielded just one show.
	

	Then there’s the issue of security and privacy for the Sussexes while in the U.K. It has long been a sore spot for Harry that while in the country, he has not been given the official police protection afforded to working royals (Harry’s cousins do not get protection). In California, the family hired their own private security team.

	Last year, Harry lost a legal battle for higher security protections in the U.K., and told the BBC: “I can’t see a world in which I would bring my wife and children back to the U.K. at this point.” Perhaps something has now changed, although U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Thursday that he hasn’t been made privy to any decision on security matters — nor would he be as that is decided by the Royal and VIP Executive Committee, an independent body. “It’s a matter for Harry and for Meghan, and we wish them well in the move that they are making,” Burnham said (via BBC). 

	The couple’s move is also somewhat surprising as just last month Harry lost his long-running privacy case against Associated Newspapers, the publisher of the tabloid Daily Mail. He was among a group of high-profile figures, including Elton John and Elizabeth Hurley, who accused the publication of unlawful information gathering, including phone-hacking. Associated Newspapers strongly denied this, and ultimately a judge ruled that the plaintiffs failed to prove their claims. Along with the other claimants, he’s expected to have to pay a hefty sum, which will be decided at a hearing on a later date. 

	It’s one of several privacy lawsuits Harry brought against tabloids over the past few years concerning his treatment in the media, and with the couple back on U.K. soil, it’s possible that this could become an issue once again. 

	Bundock points out that the couple have not always helped themselves by airing their many grievances in public, whether it was their Oprah interview, their six-part Netflix series “Harry & Meghan” or Harry’s memoir, all of which contained deeply intimate details about life within the royal family, who for the most part remain beloved — or at least respected — in the U.K. “The way they’ve aired these very personal grievances so publicly caused absolutely catastrophic problems and created such suspicion and mistrust, not just within the family but within the wider public as well,” she says. “So they’ve got work to do, winning over everyone.”

	Tennis has never been more in fashion.

	On-court (and court-side) style will be on full display when the U.S Open returns to Flushing this weekend. Defending champions Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka headline a field that also includes Coco Gauff, Novak Djokovic, Jessica Pegula and Ben Shelton.

	Earlier this year, the ATP launched “Athlete Arrivals,” tennis’s version of the NBA tunnel walk that gives players a dedicated fashion moment before matches, enlisting former GQ fashion director Mobolaji Dawodu to style stars including Taylor Fritz, Frances Tiafoe and Alexander Zverev. The initiative grew out of an ATP Styling Studio first tested ahead of last year’s U.S Open.


	What can we expect from arrivals? Preppy tennis-white uniforms have given way to retro polos, micro shorts, ’90s color blocking and Y2K-inspired kits. And there will be no shortage of luxury brands. Fashion houses have increased their relationship with the sport, signing stars including Sinner and Sabalenka with Gucci, Alcaraz with Louis Vuitton and Gauff with Miu Miu.

	Performance brands are mining their archives, too. Adidas has rolled out three heritage-driven collections for the U.S. hard-court season, including New York kits slated for Jessica Pegula and Alexander Zverev; New Balance has introduced a dedicated NYC capsule alongside fresh colorways of Gauff’s signature shoes; Wilson’s “Always New York” collection channels classic American tennis through a downtown New York lens; and Lululemon, which has been testing its first sweat-concealing ShowZero technology on Tiafoe. 


	Even jewelry brands have gotten in on the action. On Thursday morning, the California-based Gorjana  announced 18-year-old tennis standout Iva Jovic as the newest face of Gorjana Sports Club, launching this adorable tennis ball necklace charm.

            Miss Grand USA has yanked Mekyla Li's crown just one week into her reign ... amid some serious legal drama surrounding the beauty queen.
      
    
            The pageant organization announced Wednesday that it was terminating Mekyla's reign and releasing her from the Miss Grand USA title and all associated duties ... saying the decision was made in accordance with its contractual policies. PEOPLE was first to report. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The organization didn't specifically say what triggered Mekyla's sudden dethroning ... but she's reportedly facing two felony hit-and-run charges stemming from a November 2024 crash in Los Angeles.
      

            Mekyla was arrested days after the crash and later pleaded not guilty.
      
    
            She's also being sued over the wreck ... with a woman claiming Mekyla caused the crash, left her seriously injured, and took off in a rideshare without calling 911.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            There's another potential pageant problem, too ... Mekyla reportedly was married from 2018 to 2019 -- and rules state contestants cannot be or have previously been married or pregnant.
      
    
            Mekyla had only been crowned Miss Grand USA on Aug. 12 ... and was still celebrating the win on Instagram the day before the organization pulled the plug.
      
    
            Talk about a short reign ... the crown was on and off in seven days.

            Brian Hickerson is breaking his silence following the death of Hayden Panettiere ... but he isn't saying much.
      
    
            Brian's attorney, Sloan Ellis from the Ellis Hinton law firm, tells TMZ ... "Hayden's death remains under investigation and it is important to allow that investigation to proceed."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The statement continues ... "As has been publicly reported, police confirmed there were no signs of foul play."
      
    
            It ends ... "Out of respect for Hayden's loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time."
      

                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Ellis is a former federal prosecutor who has worked hand-in-hand with the DEA and FBI on past cases ... which is notable, considering we first reported that the DEA has joined the multi-agency investigation.
      
    
            As we first told you ... Brian and his brother, Zach Hickerson, were both at the South Carolina apartment when Hayden died. Brian was asleep in the other room and Zach came in to find her unresponsive on an armchair.
      
    
            First responders tried to save her, but she was ultimately pronounced dead at the scene ... and Brian reportedly became visibly emotional as efforts to save her came to an end.
      
    
            Police say Brian showed them a bag of medications Hayden was taking before she died.
      
    
            Brian and Hayden had a long, complicated history together.
      
    
            The two began dating in 2018, and their relationship later became the subject of multiple domestic violence cases involving Brian.
      
    
            Brian isn't saying all that much here ... as investigators continue trying to piece together what happened leading up to Hayden's death.
